entry.title: INKLUDE to THRIVE Programme | King's College London

media:group.media:title: INKLUDE to THRIVE Programme | King's College London
media:group.media:description:
INKLUDE to THRIVE is part of the Wellcome Trust funded INKLUDE Research Culture project, a personal and professional development offer for women and ethnically mioritised groups at King's, co-designed by its participants.
It has engaged more than 200 individuals, including 40 of King's leaders, and fostered a strong and unique community of academics, researchers and professional service staff from all roles across the entire university.
To find out more about visit: https://www.kcl.ac.uk/research/inklude

entry.title: Experts on: Dr Clement Sefa-Nyarko on critical minerals

media:group.media:title: Experts on: Dr Clement Sefa-Nyarko on critical minerals
media:group.media:description:
What are critical minerals?
In the latest episode of Experts On, Dr Clement Sefa-Nyarko, Senior Lecturer in Security at the African Leadership Centre, explains why these minerals are essential to the technologies we rely on every day and are key to the global transition to net zero.
But while demand continues to grow, access to critical minerals, and the benefits they generate, remain unevenly distributed around the world.
Watch the full video to learn more.

entry.title: Experts On: Dr Jack Brown talks devolution

media:group.media:title: Experts On: Dr Jack Brown talks devolution
media:group.media:description:
Could giving communities more power be the change Britain needs?
In this latest episode of Experts On, we're joined by Dr Jack Brown, Senior Lecturer in Government Studies at King’s College London’s Policy Institute, to discuss how national debt limits the government’s room to act and why shifting power from Westminster to local communities could be long overdue.
So, what do you think? Is it time to shift more power out of Westminster? Let us know in the comments.

entry.title: The Doctor Who Wants Every Community to Feel Seen | Anton Beka | King’s College London

media:group.media:title: The Doctor Who Wants Every Community to Feel Seen | Anton Beka | King’s College London
media:group.media:description:
“I want to be the voice for people in the community who are unheard.” 🩺
Meet Anton Beka, a King’s College London medical graduate whose journey into medicine is rooted in representation, community and a commitment to making healthcare more inclusive.
As the son of refugees, Anton understands the importance of trust and understanding between healthcare professionals and the communities they serve.
Through his work, including founding the Move Mountains Foundation, Anton is helping to bridge gaps in healthcare by supporting medical education initiatives and creating opportunities for communities that face greater barriers.
In this episode of King’s College London calling , he reflects the importance of having doctors who not only provide care, but also understand the experiences and challenges that shape people’s health. Six voices. Six paths. One connection. This is King's College London Calling.
#kingscollegelondon #medicine #healthcare #medicaleducation #WideningParticipation #HealthEquity #CommunityHealth #FutureDoctors
